description: The plot titled “Training Loss of 20M Data Size” illustrates training loss as a function of training step for six model configurations (ChemBART, ChemBERTa, and ChemLLaMA; each in Small and Medium sizes) using a 20M dataset. The x-axis is labeled “Step,” uses a linear scale, and is shown with a broken axis: the main left segment spans from 0k to 80k with labeled ticks at 0k, 20k, 40k, 60k, and 80k, and a right segment spans from 420k to 440k with labeled ticks at 420k, 430k, and 440k. The y-axis is labeled “Train Loss,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 0.85, with labeled ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.75, and 0.85. All six series are drawn as thin solid lines with no markers: ChemBART Small 20M (red) starts near about 0.8 at the earliest steps, drops rapidly below ~0.4 within the first few thousand steps, then declines more gradually to around ~0.15 by ~80k and is around ~0.04–0.05 in the 420k–440k window; ChemBART Medium 20M (blue) follows a similar shape, beginning near ~0.8, falling quickly early on, reaching roughly ~0.12–0.14 by ~80k, and ending near ~0.03–0.04 by ~440k; ChemBERTa Small 20M (green) begins near ~0.8, decreases steeply early, sits around ~0.16–0.18 by ~80k, and is around ~0.05–0.06 by ~440k; ChemBERTa Medium 20M (orange) starts near ~0.8, drops quickly at low steps, is around ~0.11–0.13 by ~80k, and is near ~0.03–0.04 by ~440k; ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple) begins near ~0.8, declines sharply early, reaches roughly ~0.09–0.11 by ~80k, and is around ~0.02–0.03 by ~440k; ChemLLaMA Medium 20M (brown) starts near ~0.8, falls quickly in the initial steps, is around ~0.07–0.09 by ~80k, and is near ~0.01–0.02 by ~440k.
caption_used: Training Loss vs. Steps for Each Model Type by Model Size with a Data Size of 20 million. The loss trends for 10 million and 20 million datasets are similar. The ChemBERTa Small 20M model exhibits the steepest decline in training loss, reaching approximately 0.15 at 440k steps. ChemLLaMA Medium 20M consistently outperforms ChemBART Medium 20M, achieving the lowest loss of all models at 0.01. The ChemBART Small 20M model shows a slower rate of decline compared to ChemLLaMA Small 20M, stabilizing at around 0.25 at 440k steps.
